title: Capacity requisition orchestration & SLA escrow pipeline
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Implement a coordinated capacity requisition pipeline that ties customer reservation requests to a verifiable SLA escrow and autoscaling policy templates. Goals: 1) enable deterministic throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers via a reservation lifecycle (request -> validation -> approval -> provisioning -> post-provision monitoring), 2) attach an SLA escrow record (terms, allowed burst, fallbacks) to every approved reservation, 3) surface operator controls in the Console to adjust or revoke reservations with clear audit trails, and 4) provide autoscaling policy defaults and override hooks that respect SLA tiers. This ticket covers API contract changes, Console intake UX, approval workflows, operator playbooks, and end-to-end telemetry requirements for capacity forecasting and reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Reservation API endpoint accepts structured requisitions with throughput_target and fallback_variants and returns idempotent reservation IDs
Approval workflow supports staged approvals: auto-approve for low-risk requests, manual approval queue for >X throughput or risky customers
SLA escrow record (JSON) is generated on approval, stored in audit logs, and surfaced in Console with term, commitment window, and breach actions
Console view shows reservation status, current utilization, projected runway, and a single-click revoke/modify action for operators
Autoscale policy templates (economy/standard/premium) available at provisioning time and honored by fleet controllers; policies include burst caps and cooldowns
Metrics emitted for every reservation lifecycle event (requested, validated, approved, provisioned, scaled, revoked) and visible in runtime dashboards
Security review signed off and KMS keyproof included for SLA escrow encryption
End-to-end e2e test that simulates a reservation request, approval, provisioning, enforced throughput limit, and graceful fallback to a lower-tier model under overload

notes: Trade-offs: we can either enforce hard throughput limits via runtime throttling (strong isolation but higher risk of customer errors) or soft guarantees with billing credits on breach (better user UX, more complex accounting). Recommended approach for pilot: hard limits for Premium tier, soft guarantees for Standard with automatic fallback. Operator controls must be reversible and logged. Need to reconcile pricing with Sales before GA.
